title: 〜を境に(して)
meaning: from (that point) on; with … as the dividing line; before and after …
simpleExplanation: 〜を境に draws a line at one point in time or space and says that things on one side are different from things on the other. 境 (さかい) means "boundary". Before X it was one way; after X (or beyond X) it is another way.
whenUsed: Mainly written and semi-formal spoken Japanese: essays, news, biographies, and explanations of change. Used with turning points in a life (四十歳・結婚・事件) or physical boundaries (川・山・国境). Neutral in tone; the change can be good or bad.
formation: Typical nouns: 事件・事故・年齢 (四十歳)・日付 (その日)・川・山脈・線

diagram.title: Before and after the boundary (この事件を境に)

items.label: before
items.description: his life as it used to be

examples.ja: この事件を境に、彼の人生は大きく変わった。
examples.reading: このじけんをさかいに、かれのじんせいはおおきくかわった。
examples.en: From this incident on, his life changed dramatically.
examples.note: The incident is a dividing line between his old life and his new one.

examples.ja: 四十歳を境に、体力が急に落ちた。
examples.reading: よんじゅっさいをさかいに、たいりょくがきゅうにおちた。
examples.en: After turning forty, my strength dropped suddenly.
examples.note: Ages are common boundaries: before forty and after forty are contrasted.

examples.ja: この川を境にして、気候が大きく異なる。
examples.reading: このかわをさかいにして、きこうがおおきくことなる。
examples.en: With this river as the dividing line, the climate differs greatly.
examples.note: With a place (川), the boundary is spatial: climate on one side vs the other.

examples.ja: その日を境に、彼女は一度も笑わなくなった。
examples.reading: そのひをさかいに、かのじょはいちどもわらわなくなった。
examples.en: From that day on, she never smiled again.
examples.note: その日を境に is a frequent narrative phrase.

examples.ja: この線を境として、市の管理区域と県の管理区域が分かれている。
examples.reading: このせんをさかいとして、しのかんりくいきとけんのかんりくいきがわかれている。
examples.en: This line is the boundary between the area managed by the city and that managed by the prefecture.
examples.note: を境として: formal, spatial boundary in official writing.

similarGrammar.difference: An occasion someone used to start a new action. を境に only observes that things differ before and after a point; nobody has to decide anything.
Also "ever since", but attaches to a verb and stresses the continuing new state with emotion. を境に attaches to a noun and stresses the contrast between two sides.
Simply "since"; the change is not necessarily contrasted with what came before.

commonMistakes.wrong: 四十歳を境に、少しずつ白髪が増えてきた。
commonMistakes.right: 四十歳を過ぎてから、少しずつ白髪が増えてきた。
commonMistakes.why: を境に implies a clear break, not a gradual drift. For a slow change use 〜てから or 〜につれて.

commonMistakes.wrong: 結婚を境にして、家を買った。
commonMistakes.right: 結婚を機に、家を買った。
commonMistakes.why: Buying a house is a single deliberate action. を境に needs a lasting difference between before and after; use を機に for a triggered action.

commonMistakes.wrong: この川に境に、気候が変わる。
commonMistakes.right: この川を境に、気候が変わる。
commonMistakes.why: The particle is を. The pattern is fixed as を境に(して).

usageNotes: The clause after を境に usually describes a lasting change: 〜ようになった, 〜なくなった, 〜が変わった.
Spatial uses (川・山・国境を境に) are neutral descriptions of geography, not changes over time.
Adding して or として makes the phrase heavier and more formal; plain を境に is fine in most writing.
jlptTips: In 文法形式の判断, a noun that is a point in time or space followed by a contrast (before ≠ after) signals を境に.
The usual distractors are を機に and をもって. If the main clause is a state that changed (変わった・なくなった), pick を境に; if it is a chosen action, pick を機に.
In 並べ替え, place を境に right after the boundary noun, and put the changed state at the end.
